scenario: AITA for ignoring my senior associate’s text | Just to give a background story, I’m a first year associate at a local firm and the senior associate in this story has been with the firm for 3 years. So a few weeks ago, I was feeling a little bit under the weather and threw up as soon as I woke up. I notified my senior associate and told her that I won’t be coming to work as I’m not feeling well. She was a bit disappointed but had no choice but to allow me a sick leave. I sent a few emails to our client as per requested by her the previous day and tried to get some sleep. As I’m trying to get some sleep, she kept on texting me with things that I needed to do. I tried to ignore it and turned off my phone’s notification so I can get some sleep. Around an hour later, she called me and told me that I have to sent her a file (regarding client’s data which she doesn’t have on her laptop) immediately as it is an urgent matter. I sent her the files she wanted and asked her if she’ll need anything else as I’m going to the doctor and won’t be bringing my laptop with me. She said that’s all for now. I went to the doctor, and the doctor said I’m overworked (I’ve been working overtime till 2-3AM for the past 2 months) and needs some rest. On my way home, my senior again texted me and told me to get our client’s billing information (something that she could do herself as she also have their contacts). I did as I’m told as fowarded her with the information. I got home, took the prescribed medicine and fell asleep. I was shocked when I woke up to find my phone with 2 miscalled and 30 new messages from her giving me work to do from home. I felt it was a little bit unfair of her to give me work while I’m on a sick leave and so I ignored the message and didn’t reply her. So, AITA for not replying her text? Notes: English is not my first language, I’m sorry if there’s a lot of grammatical errors.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to ignore my senior associate's texts while I was on sick leave. Let me break this down step by step. First, I was feeling unwell, threw up, and notified my senior associate that I wouldn't be coming to work. She was disappointed but allowed me sick leave. That seems reasonable because I was genuinely sick. I sent some emails as she requested and tried to rest, which is important when you're feeling ill. But then, she started texting me with tasks. I tried to ignore her and turned off notifications to get some sleep. An hour later, she called and said it was urgent, needing some files. I sent them and asked if she needed anything else, explaining I was going to the doctor and wouldn't bring my laptop. She said that was all for now. After the doctor's visit, she texted again asking for billing information, which I provided. On my way home, she messaged me again with more work. I did it, but when I got home, she sent 30 messages with work tasks. I felt it was unfair to give me work while I was on sick leave, so I ignored the messages. Now, I'm wondering if ignoring her texts was the right thing to do. Let me consider the factors: 1. **Health and Well-being**: I was sick and overworked. The doctor said I needed rest. Ignoring texts allowed me to recover, which is crucial for my health and to prevent burnout. 2. **Workload and Expectations**: She kept assigning tasks even when I was out. It's possible she didn't realize the extent of my illness or the impact of her requests. However, as a senior associate, she should understand the importance of respecting sick leave. 3. **Professional Boundaries**: Ignoring her texts set a boundary. It's important to communicate when you're unable to work, but in this case, I had already informed her I was sick. Continuing to work while unwell could have worsened my condition. 4. **Impact on Work**: By ignoring the texts, I might have caused delays, but I was already providing necessary information when possible. It's a balance between rest and fulfilling responsibilities. 5. **Communication**: Maybe I should have responded to clarify that I was unable to work due to illness and that she should handle urgent matters without me. But given my state, it was hard to communicate effectively. 6. **Company Policies**: I should check if there are policies about sick leave and work during that period. If the company expects employees to handle urgent tasks even when sick, that's a different scenario. But if not, ignoring the texts was appropriate. 7. **Work-Life Balance**: This situation highlights the importance of work-life balance. Overworking leads to illness, and not being able to rest properly can create a cycle of poor health and decreased productivity. In conclusion, while ignoring the texts might seem like not fulfilling my duties, considering my health and the fact that I had already communicated my unavailability, it was a necessary step to recover and prevent further issues. It's also a sign that the work environment might need better support for employees' well-being.
